deep.reconstruction:
Context: in E260 Euler models fluid friction against a wall as proportional to the normal pressure, like Coulomb friction, with coefficient alpha. Applied to a pipe of constant cross-section g^2 (g = square root of the area), the steady-flow momentum balance becomes a linear first-order ODE in the pressure head along the pipe. Integrating it gives an exponential attenuation factor exp(-alpha*b/g) over a pipe of length b. The preceding sections (103-104) had already shown numerically that jet height depends on pipe width and length, not only on reservoir height.

This page opens an Appendix on fountains ('fontes salientes', Tab. VII Fig. 5). It specialises the general result to the usual design case.
- Assumptions: the water depth in the reservoir, AB = a, is negligible compared with the reservoir's elevation above the nozzle DD. The nozzle tube CD is short and wide enough that the friction quantity (printed alpha c / b, presumably c being the nozzle length) is negligible.
- Result (sec. 105): the height due to the exit velocity, i.e. the vertical jet height, is v = (g cos(zeta)/alpha)(1 - e^{-alpha b/g}) - l(1 - e^{-alpha b/g}). Here l is the water-column height equivalent to atmospheric pressure (about 30 ft) and zeta is the inclination of the main pipe BE to the vertical. The atmospheric term enters because the friction is proportional to total (absolute) pressure.
- Sec. 106: for a straight pipe, b cos(zeta) = q, the head CF of the reservoir above the fountain. Hence v = (g q/(alpha b) - l)(1 - e^{-alpha b/g}).
- Sec. 107 begins: the pipe is cylindrical with constant section g^2.

The next page completes the programme:
- g^2 = (pi/4) d^2 and alpha = 1/4540, so g/alpha is about 4023 d, taken as 4000 d.
- Expanding the exponential gives v = (q - alpha b l/g)(1 - x/2 + x^2/6 - ...) with x = alpha b/g = n/4000 and n = b/d.
- This yields a practical engineering rule, v = N q - M, where N = (1 - e^{-x})/x is a function of the length/diameter ratio alone.

Checks:
- As alpha -> 0, v -> q, the frictionless Torricelli limit.
- The jet vanishes when q/b < alpha l/g, a finite slope threshold that is an artifact of the pressure-proportional friction law.
- The algebra on the page is correct given Euler's model.
errors: Physical: the friction law (wall friction proportional to normal/absolute pressure) is wrong for water in pipes. Real head loss depends on velocity (Chezy 1769/1775, Darcy-Weisbach 1845); Euler's law makes the loss independent of discharge.
Consequently the atmospheric pressure l spuriously reduces the jet height. In reality atmospheric pressure acts equally at the reservoir surface and the jet exit and cancels.
The model predicts a spurious threshold: no jet at all when the pipe slope q/b < alpha*l/g, however large q is in absolute terms.

The printed smallness condition 'alpha c / b' for the nozzle tube CD looks dimensionally odd if b is the main pipe length. One would expect alpha*c divided by the nozzle's width, so this is possibly a misprint or a reuse of letters from the earlier sections. Unsure.

Neighbouring page: the rule 'v = Nq - (1/400) N n' with l = 30 ft and g/alpha = 4000 d should read (30/4000) N n = (3/400) N n. Either the transcription or the print has dropped a factor 3. This needs checking against the image of p. 380.
Alpha is quoted as 1/4549 on p. 378 and 1/4540 on p. 380: an internal inconsistency or a misprint.

ideas.what: Pressure-proportional (Coulomb-type) wall friction in pipe flow, producing exponential decay of available head along a straight pipe of length b
ideas.modern_name: Coulomb friction law applied to fluids; head loss in pipes (superseded by Darcy-Weisbach)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler himself (E260) as an early, incorrect friction theory; correct pipe-loss laws to Chezy, Prony, Darcy, Weisbach
ideas.where_published: E260, Novi Comment. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 6 (1756/7, publ. 1761); Opera omnia II.13 (unsure of exact volume)

ideas.what: Jet height of a fountain fed by a long pipe from a reservoir: v = (gq/(alpha b) - l)(1 - e^{-alpha b/g})
ideas.modern_name: Fountain jet height with pipe head loss (energy/Bernoulli equation with friction loss)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hydraulic practice (Mariotte for fountain jets; later Bossut, Prony)

ideas.what: Jet-height reduction depends only on the ratio n = pipe length / pipe diameter (via g/alpha = 4000 d)
ideas.modern_name: L/D dependence of friction head loss (Darcy-Weisbach h_f = f (L/D) V^2/2g)

missed.claim: Euler gives a practical design rule in which fountain head loss scales with the pipe's length-to-diameter ratio n = L/d, with an empirically fitted constant (about 4000). This predates Chezy and Darcy-Weisbach. Histories of pipe-flow hydraulics (e.g. Rouse and Ince) usually do not mention Euler's L/d rule, though Truesdell's fluid-mechanics surveys likely note E260's friction hypothesis.
missed.quote: erit b cos. zeta altitudo aquae in castello supra fontem ... sicque erit v = (gq/(alpha b) - l)(1 - e^{-alpha b/g})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest only: a mid-18th-century, empirically calibrated L/d head-loss rule. The underlying physics is wrong, so it has no modern technical value.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine specialisation of Euler's (known, physically incorrect) pressure-proportional friction theory to fountains. The only mildly notable point is the early L/d scaling of the loss with an empirical constant, which may be under-credited in hydraulics histories.
transcription_corrections: Margin note reads 'Tab. VII Fig. 5.' (correctly captured).
In sec. 105 the condition is printed as 'alpha c / b'. The transcription follows the print, but the intended denominator may be the nozzle width rather than b.
